paper.title: Algorithm 837: AMD, an approximate minimum degree ordering algorithm

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 837.zip (re-fetched 2026-11-26 19:34Z, sha256 d15f725ac0a540a4830972fd4b503669121ae9bd26fb0539c94cc4860f72d96a); the demo output file Demo/amd_demo.out (sha256 63a791ae537cb1126fad775dbc9a629a8787568812f8cc47f1a3bf660c9702f0) is inside it; the first registration hash f9ae8b20... was from an earlier netlib download of the same archive (repacked; the inner Demo/amd_demo.out is byte-identical, sha256 63a791ae... both times)
code.note: AMD 1.1 (C and Fortran versions). The demo Demo/amd_demo.c runs AMD on the built-in 24-by-24 Harwell/Boeing matrix can_24 and prints statistics; build with make in Source and the demo via make fortran or the C demo target. Needs a C compiler (gcc); the Fortran demo needs a Fortran compiler. The archive's README says 'Copyright (c) 2004'.

claim.location: The archive's shipped output of the C demo, Demo/amd_demo.out, section 'amd: approximate minimum degree ordering, results' for can_24: 'LDL' flop count for real A: 647'.

reference.file: 837/Demo/amd_demo.out, line containing "LDL' flop count for real A"

claim.metric: The 'LDL' flop count for real A' integer printed by amd_demo for the can_24 matrix, compared with the shipped value 647 (exact integer equality).
claim.paper_value: Not used: the paper is paywalled (ACM DL) and was not read, so the claim rests on the shipped demo output alone.

values.name: LDL' flop count for real A, can_24 demo (amd_demo.out)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The value is an exact integer from a deterministic ordering and symbolic count, so the tolerance is exact equality. A mismatch is a finding to diagnose (compiler, version, tie-breaking), not a licence to loosen it.

cost.data_size: None; the 24x24 matrix can_24 is built into the demo source.
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence of the archive; the rerun should record the licence text in the archive README.

why: AMD is a sparse ordering code whose demo prints exact integer factorisation counts for a fixed matrix; the count needs the ordering and the symbolic factor to be computed, not a closed form, and it is exact so any drift is visible.
